name: Raghurajpur Heritage Crafts Village
summary: World-renowned artisan village where every household preserves the age-old master craft of Pattachitra cloth paintings.
description: Nestled amidst coconut and palm groves 14 km from Puri, Raghurajpur is India's premier heritage crafts village. Every villager is an artisan specializing in Pattachitra (cloth-based scroll painting with mineral pigments), palm leaf carvings (Talapatra Chitra), cow dung toys, and wood sculptures. It is also the birthplace of legendary Odissi maestro Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra and the traditional Gotipua dance.

name: Jagannath Temple
summary: Sacred 12th-century temple of Lord Jagannath, one of the four Char Dham pilgrimage sites, celebrated for the mega Rath Yatra.
description: Constructed by King Anantavarman Chodaganga Deva in the 12th century, this iconic temple enshrines Lord Jagannath along with brother Balabhadra and sister Subhadra. The temple is famous for its towering 65-meter deula, mysterious flag fluttering opposite to wind direction, the world's largest kitchen (Ananda Bazar) preparing Mahaprasad, and the internationally celebrated annual Chariot Festival (Ratha Yatra).

name: Puri Beach
summary: Golden sandy shore on the Bay of Bengal, famous for dramatic sunrises, sacred pilgrim bathing, and sand art.
description: Puri Beach (Golden Beach) is one of the most vibrant coastlines in Eastern India, certified with the prestigious Blue Flag tag at designated stretches for impeccable cleanliness and safety. Renowned globally for intricate sand sculptures by Padma Shri Sudarsan Pattnaik, evening seafood stalls, and lively beach markets.

name: Konark Sun Temple
summary: Monumental 13th-century UNESCO World Heritage Sun Temple sculpted as a gigantic cosmic stone chariot.
description: Built in 1250 AD by King Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga Dynasty, Konark Sun Temple is an architectural summit of ancient Kalinga stonecraft. Designed as a mammoth chariot of the Sun God Surya, it features 24 exquisitely carved 12-spoked wheels acting as accurate astronomical sundials and seven horses galloping towards the dawn.

name: Chilika Lake
summary: Asia's largest coastal lagoon and Ramsar Wetland site, famous for playful Irrawaddy dolphins and migratory birds.
description: Chilika Lake covers over 1,100 square kilometers across three districts of Odisha. It supports one of the world's only two surviving populations of Irrawaddy dolphins, predominantly spotted at Satapada. During winter, Nalabana Island becomes host to over one million migratory birds arriving from Siberia, Mongolia, and Central Asia.

name: Udayagiri and Khandagiri Caves
summary: Historic rock-cut cave complexes carved in the 1st-2nd century BCE under Emperor Kharavela for Jain monks.
description: The twin hills of Udayagiri (Sunrise Hill) and Khandagiri (Broken Hill) feature 33 partly artificial rock-cut caverns built during the Chedi dynasty. Udayagiri contains the famous Rani Gumpha (Queen's Cave) with two-storey reliefs, and Hathigumpha featuring the 17-line Brahmi inscription chronicling the military expeditions and civic works of King Kharavela.

name: Dhauli Shanti Stupa
summary: Striking white peace pagoda atop Dhauli Hills marking Ashoka's conversion to Buddhism and non-violence.
description: Dhauli Shanti Stupa sits beside the Daya River where the monumental Kalinga War occurred in 261 BCE. Seeing the river turn crimson with bloodshed, Emperor Ashoka renounced conquest by war (Digvijaya) in favor of conquest through dharma (Dharmavijaya). The stupa was built jointly in 1972 by the Kalinga Nippon Buddha Sangha and the Government of Odisha.

name: Lingaraj Temple
summary: Majestic 11th-century temple representing the pinnacle of mature Kalinga architecture, dedicated to Lord Harihara.
description: The largest temple in Bhubaneswar, Lingaraj Temple stands inside a spacious compound with 108 subsidiary shrines. The central deula rises to an imposing 55 meters and is dedicated to Tribhuvaneswara (Lord of Three Worlds, Shiva combined with Vishnu as Harihara). The complex overlooks the sacred Bindusagar Lake.

name: Nandankanan Zoological Park
summary: Internationally celebrated zoological garden nestled around Kanjia Lake, famous for white tigers and lion safaris.
description: Nandankanan, literally meaning "Garden of Heavens", covers 437 hectares across the Chandaka forest. It was the first zoo in the world where white tigers were bred in captivity and the first to breed Indian pangolins successfully. Features open-moated enclosures, ropeway over the lake, nocturnal animal house, and boat safaris.

name: Barabati Fort
summary: 14th-century medieval citadel on the Mahanadi River, featuring an ornate stone gateway, deep moat, and earthen ramparts.
description: Built by the Ganga dynasty in the 14th century, Barabati Fort protected the strategic delta capital of Cuttack. Surviving remnants include an impressive arched gateway decorated with fine stone relief carvings, a moat, and the stone foundations of an ancient nine-storey palace described enthusiastically in Persian chronicles.

name: Similipal National Park
summary: UNESCO Biosphere Reserve boasting lush Sal forest ranges, rare pseudo-melanistic black tigers, and cascading waterfalls.
description: Covering 2,750 square kilometers, Similipal is the 7th largest national park in India. Named after the red silk cotton (Semul) trees that blossom here, it features dramatic escarpments, Barehipani Falls (399m) and Joranda Falls (150m), and is the only habitat on Earth hosting wild pseudo-melanistic Royal Bengal tigers.

name: Bhitarkanika National Park
summary: Vibrant mangrove estuary and Ramsar site sheltering India's largest population of giant saltwater crocodiles.
description: Bhitarkanika is India's second largest mangrove ecosystem after the Sundarbans, created by the rivers Brahmani, Baitarani, and Dhamra. The park is home to over 1,700 saltwater crocodiles (including record-holding specimens exceeding 20 feet), king cobras, spotted deer, wild boars, and 215 bird species.

name: Gopalpur Beach
summary: Historic maritime commercial seaport and tranquil beach getaway renowned for its 1871 lighthouse and casuarina groves.
description: Gopalpur-on-Sea was a bustling commercial sea port during the British and Kalinga maritime eras, trading silk and rice with Burma. Today it is a peaceful, uncrowded beach destination featuring scenic casuarina plantations, a historic operational lighthouse with panoramic coast views, and golden sunrises.

name: Daringbadi
summary: Idyllic highland hill station named the "Kashmir of Odisha", featuring pine groves, coffee plantations, and winter frost.
description: Perched at an elevation of 915 meters in the Eastern Ghats of Kandhamal, Daringbadi is the only place in Odisha that occasionally experiences sub-zero temperatures and winter ground frost. Attractions include dense pine forests, lush organic coffee plantations, Hill View Point, Midubanda Waterfall, and vibrant tribal villages.

name: Hirakud Dam
summary: Engineering marvel across the Mahanadi River, the world's longest earthen dam stretching 25.8 kilometers.
description: Constructed between 1948 and 1957 as India's first major multipurpose river valley project after independence, Hirakud Dam forms a massive reservoir covering 743 square kilometers. Visitors can ascend Gandhi Minar and Nehru Minar watchtowers for breathtaking 360-degree views of the waters and surrounding Barapahad hills.
